# ACR drift report — RiverCity Metro Rider Portal

**Documents compared:** `rcm-2026q3` (v1, issued 2026-07-28, product 2026.3) → `rcm-2027q1` (v2, issued 2027-02-19, product 2027.1)
**Evaluator, both cycles:** Meridian Digital Accessibility (Dana Okafor)
**Prepared for:** RiverCity Metro Authority, Office of Civil Rights

**Basis.** This is a re-reading of two finished, delivered documents plus the current cycle's delivered re-check table and the two engagement sample records. No testing was performed for this request. Nothing below is new evidence; where a conclusion is my inference rather than a statement carried by the delivered documents, it is marked as such.

---

## The short version

The single worst thing in the 2026.3 report is gone, and the portal got broader-but-shallower problems in its place. A rider using a keyboard could not complete a fare purchase in 2026.3; they can now. Meanwhile the missing skip-link target spread from two peripheral pages to half the sample — including the schedules and account areas riders use most — and a new station-detail template shipped with focus-obscuring behaviour.

Those two movements are not on the same axis, and the row counts flatten them. A blocked purchase is a total task failure; a dead skip link is repeated friction on every page load. The report is genuinely better at the place a rider was stopped outright, and genuinely worse across the pages a rider touches most often. Do not compress that into "net improvement."

Three headline numbers, each of which misleads on its own:

- **Open findings 7 → 5.** True, but 4 of the 5 still open are carry-overs from the prior cycle. Only one is new. Remediation this cycle was concentrated entirely on the checkout process.
- **MAJOR count 4 → 4.** Flat, but the composition turned over: two closed, two persisted, one was promoted in from MINOR, one is new.
- **`does-not-support` rows 1 → 1.** Flat, but it moved from a Level AA criterion (1.3.5) to a Level A criterion (2.4.1). Against a WCAG 2.2 AA target both are failures of the target; on a published ACR, a Level A outright non-support row reads very differently.

---

## What did not move (the comparison is valid)

A drift report is worthless if the yardstick moved. It did not:

- **Conformance target:** WCAG 2.2 Level AA, both cycles.
- **Catalog:** `2.5-edition-wcag-2.2-508-en`, both cycles — the same 56 rows (32 Level A + 24 Level AA, including the retained 4.1.1 row that WCAG 2.2 removed).
- **Scope boundary:** web component only, both cycles. All four disabled chapters (functional performance criteria, hardware, software, support documentation and services) carry byte-identical boundary notes. The RideRC native app and the PDF timetables are outside both documents in exactly the same way.
- **Evaluator and reporting lead:** unchanged, so no inter-rater shift needs to be accounted for.
- **Method family:** WCAG-EM 2.0 both cycles; 11 structured + 1 random + 2 complete processes both cycles.
- **AAA chapter:** empty in both, same rationale.

---

## 1. Document metadata

| Field | rcm-2026q3 | rcm-2027q1 |
|---|---|---|
| `product.version` | 2026.3 | 2027.1 |
| `report_date` | 2026-07-28 | 2027-02-19 |
| `version` | 1 | 2 |
| `evaluation_methods_used` | WCAG-EM 2.0; 11 + 1 + 2 | WCAG-EM 2.0 **re-evaluation**; 11 + 1 + 2; **7 structured samples and P01 carried over from rcm-2026q3 for comparability** |
| `title`, `product.name`, `author`, `legal_disclaimer`, `notes`, `catalog` | — | unchanged, verbatim |

Two things in that table need action, both flagged in section 7: the carry-over statement does not match the engagement record, and the legal disclaimer still says "Draft for review" on a version-2 document.

---

## 2. Row-level drift

**49 of 56 rows are byte-identical.** Seven rows changed text; six of those changed adherence level.

| Adherence level | rcm-2026q3 | rcm-2027q1 | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|
| `supports` | 40 | 42 | +2 |
| `partially-supports` | 6 | 4 | −2 |
| `does-not-support` | 1 | 1 | 0 — but moved from Level AA to Level A |
| `not-applicable` | 9 | 9 | 0 |
| **Total** | **56** | **56** | — |

### The seven rows that changed

| SC | Level | rcm-2026q3 | rcm-2027q1 | Direction |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2.1.1 Keyboard | A | partially-supports | **supports** | Improved — finding closed |
| 2.4.1 Bypass Blocks | A | partially-supports | **does-not-support** | Worsened — finding spread, severity raised |
| 3.3.1 Error Identification | A | partially-supports | **supports** | Improved — finding closed |
| 1.3.5 Identify Input Purpose | AA | does-not-support | **partially-supports** | Improved — failing surface halved |
| 1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum) | AA | partially-supports | partially-supports | **Unchanged** — notes differ, defect does not |
| 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured (Min.) | AA | supports | **partially-supports** | New defect on a new template |
| 4.1.3 Status Messages | AA | partially-supports | **supports** | Improved — finding closed |

### A caveat that a text diff will not surface

Forty-nine rows carry identical note strings — most of them the sentence *"Sample-scoped: passes across 11 structured + 1 random samples (WCAG-EM)."* That sentence is true of both cycles and refers to **different sample sets**. Four of eleven structured samples were replaced and the random draw is a different page from a larger sitemap (section 4). Identical row text is not identical evidence, and an unchanged `supports` row is not a re-test result. The same applies to the `not-applicable` rows: *"no audio or video content exists in any sampled view"* now means a different set of views.

---

## 3. Finding-level drift — every fingerprint accounted for

| finding_id | fingerprint | SC | 2026q3 | 2027q1 | Movement |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| a11y_fare_zone_slider_keyboard | `7c1f22ab` | 2.1.1 | partially-supports / CRITICAL | — | **Closed** |
| a11y_payment_error_association | `c30e51f9` | 3.3.1 | partially-supports / MAJOR | — | **Closed** |
| a11y_purchase_confirm_silent | `e8c2447d` | 4.1.3 | partially-supports / MAJOR | — | **Closed** |
| a11y_route_badge_contrast | `2ab9d871` | 1.4.3 | partially-supports / MAJOR | partially-supports / MAJOR | Open — flat, two cycles |
| a11y_swap_button_name | `91d4e0c3` | 4.1.2 | partially-supports / MINOR | partially-supports / MINOR | Open — static |
| a11y_form_autocomplete_missing | `44b09ce6` | 1.3.5 | does-not-support / MAJOR | partially-supports / MAJOR | Open — surface reduced |
| a11y_legacy_skiplink_anchor | `5f77ab02` | 2.4.1 | partially-supports / MINOR | does-not-support / **MAJOR** | Open — surface expanded |
| a11y_sticky_filterbar_obscures_focus | `3d90c7e1` | 2.4.11 | — | partially-supports / MAJOR | **New this cycle** |

Severity ledger: CRITICAL 1 → 0; MAJOR 4 → 4; MINOR 2 → 1. The MINOR drop is not a fix — the skip-link finding left the MINOR bucket by promotion.

### Closed (3) — and the closures are the strongest evidence in the pair

All three closures sit on **carried-over surfaces**: S07 checkout and both branches of process P01. Nothing about the sample change is doing the work here; these are like-for-like re-tests of the same surfaces that failed last cycle, and the re-check table records positive verification in each case rather than absence of observation. That is as clean as re-evaluation evidence gets.

The fare-zone slider (`7c1f22ab`) was the only CRITICAL in either cycle and it blocked a complete process — a keyboard user could not buy a pass. It is now a stepper with full keyboard operation, verified in both P01 branches and a driven keyboard session. This is the most consequential single change between the two reports.

### Open and worsening (1) — this is the headline regression

`5f77ab02`, the missing skip-link target, went from failing R01 and S11 (2 of 12 samples) to failing S03, S06, S11, S12, S15 and R02 (6 of 12). Cause, per the re-check table: the legacy info-page shell was rolled out across the schedules and account areas in 2026-11.

**This is a true regression, not a sampling artifact.** S03 (route schedule) and S06 (account dashboard) are carried-over samples that passed this criterion in the prior cycle and fail it now. The same surfaces, tested twice, changed state.

The severity promotion MINOR → MAJOR is well-founded on reach rather than on a change in the defect itself. Last cycle it affected the Title VI page and one random draw — peripheral. Now it affects route schedules and the account dashboard, which is where riders spend their time, and where a rider is most likely to load page after page. Each load means tabbing the full header before reaching content, with no working bypass. *(The user-impact reading here is my inference from the finding description; the delivered documents state the surface and severity, not the interaction cost.)*

One point the row does not make on its own: the defect was hit by the random draw in **both** cycles — R01 in 2026q3 and R02 in 2027q1, independently seeded, from two different sitemaps. Two for two on random draws is a small sample, but it is directionally consistent with the template-rollout story and suggests the failure extends well beyond the structured picks into the unsampled population.

### Open and improving (1)

`44b09ce6`, missing autocomplete tokens, moved from `does-not-support` to `partially-supports` because S07 checkout now carries tokens on every applicable field. S08 — the paratransit application form — still carries none, and S08 was carried over, so nothing changed for anyone using it.

Note what did **not** move: severity is still MAJOR. Conformance level and impact severity are orthogonal, and this row is the clearest example in the pair. The document reads better; a specific rider's experience is identical.

*(Inference, not carried by the delivered documents:* of the two forms, the one still failing is the paratransit application — the form most likely to be completed by people who depend on autofill, and the one with the highest cost of abandonment. If remediation capacity is scarce, the row that improved is the wrong signal to prioritise from.*)*

### Open and flat (2)

`2ab9d871`, route-badge contrast, is the item to watch. Same shared component, same measurement (2.8:1 against a 4.5:1 requirement), same severity, two cycles running. Its failing-sample list changed from "S03 and S09" to "S03 and S15" — that is **not** movement. S09 was retired from the sample and S15 came in reusing the same badge component. A naive diff will report a changed failure surface where the defect is unchanged and merely followed its component into a new template.

That last part is the real signal: a single shared component with a two-cycle-old, one-token defect is now propagating into newly built templates. It is very likely the cheapest fix on the list and it has had no attention across two cycles while its reach grew.

`91d4e0c3`, the icon-only swap control on the trip planner, is unchanged in every respect on a carried-over sample. MINOR is defensible — the re-check notes that origin and destination fields remain directly editable, so a workaround exists.

### New (1)

`3d90c7e1`, sticky filter bar obscuring focused rows in the S14 departures table. **This is not a regression.** S14 (station detail) shipped 2026-12 and has no counterpart in the prior sample; the prior cycle's `supports` on 2.4.11 was never a statement about this template. New coverage found a new defect on new code — which is the system working, not backsliding.

---

## 4. Sample drift, and what it costs the comparison

| | rcm-2026q3 | rcm-2027q1 |
|---|---|---|
| Structured | 11 (S01–S11) | 11 (S01, S02, S03, S06, S07, S08, S11, S12, S13, S14, S15) |
| Random | R01 `/riders/lost-and-found`, seed 7391, 214-URL sitemap | R02 `/riders/bike-racks`, seed 8815, 251-URL sitemap |
| Complete processes | P01 (web), P02 (native) | P01 (web), P02 (native) |

- **Carried over:** S01, S02, S03, S06, S07, S08, S11 (7 of 11) and both complete processes.
- **Retired:** S04 service alerts, S05 fares, S09 news article, S10 accessibility policy, R01.
- **Added:** S12 alerts subscription (shipped 2026-11), S13 fare calculator (rebuilt 2026-10), S14 station detail (shipped 2026-12), S15 news index, R02.

Three consequences:

1. **Two retired samples have no stated successor.** S05 → S13 and S09 → S15 are documented replacements. S04 (service alerts) and S10 (accessibility policy) simply left. Unless those templates were retired from the product — which the engagement record does not say — the current cycle carries **no evidence** for them, and their prior-cycle `supports` rows do not carry forward. The accessibility policy page in particular is one a commissioner may not want unsampled in a published ACR. This needs a one-line rationale either way (section 7).
2. **The random draws are not comparable to each other.** Different page, different seed, different population. R01 and R02 are two independent draws, not a re-test.
3. **Coverage thinned proportionally.** The sitemap grew from 214 to 251 URLs (+17%) while the structured sample held at 11 — from roughly 5.1% to 4.4% of URLs. Not a defect in the method; worth stating so the two cycles' `supports` rows are not read as equally strong.

---

## 5. Real movement vs. sampling artifact — the separation that matters

| Change | Real, same-surface movement | Artifact of sample turnover |
|---|---|---|
| 2.1.1, 3.3.1, 4.1.3 closures | ✅ S07 and P01 carried over; verified absent | — |
| 1.3.5 improvement | ✅ S07 fixed (carried over); S08 still fails (carried over) | — |
| 2.4.1 regression | ✅ S03 and S06 carried over, passed then, fail now | Partly — S12, S15, R02 are new surfaces that add to the count |
| 1.4.3 "changed" failing samples | ❌ Nothing moved | ✅ S09 out, S15 in, same component |
| 2.4.11 new finding | ❌ Not a regression | ✅ S14 did not exist in the prior sample |
| 49 unchanged `supports` rows | Unknown | ✅ Same sentence, different sample set |

---

## 6. Pattern worth naming

Three of the four MAJORs currently open trace to the Q4 2026 template wave:

- `5f77ab02` spread via the 2026-11 legacy-shell rollout (S03, S06, S12, S15, R02).
- `3d90c7e1` arrived with the 2026-12 station-detail template (S14).
- `2ab9d871` followed its component into the new news-index template (S15).

Against that, the checkout remediation programme closed everything it targeted, including the only CRITICAL. And the wave was not uniformly bad: S13, the fare calculator rebuilt in 2026-10, carries no finding at all — so building accessibly in that window was clearly possible.

*(Inference, offered as an observation rather than an evaluator conclusion:* the pattern is consistent with remediation being handled as a project and new template work shipping without an equivalent gate. If that reading is right, the same shape will recur next cycle from whatever ships in 2027 H1, and it is a process fix rather than a defect list.*)*

---

## 7. Integrity checks and three things to fix before publication

**Clean:** the re-check table and the current ACR rows agree item for item. Every prior fingerprint is accounted for, every current row's `finding_id` and fingerprint appears in the re-check table, and no finding is orphaned in either direction. Level determinations track their stated rationales — 1.3.5 moving off `does-not-support` once one of two applicable surfaces passes, and 2.4.1 moving onto it once half the sample fails, are both consistent readings of the catalog terms.

**Needs attention:**

1. **Carry-over statement does not match the sample record.** `evaluation_methods_used` says *"7 structured samples and P01 carried over"*; the engagement record says both complete processes carried over (P01 **and** P02). The likely explanation is that the methods string is scoped to the web component and P02 is the native app — but as written the two documents disagree, and a reader checking the record will find it. One clause fixes it.
2. **"Majority of the sample" is exactly half.** The re-check table describes the skip-link failure as affecting *"the majority of the sample"*; it fails 6 of 12 samples. The ACR row's own wording — *"every template now built on the legacy shell"* — is accurate and stronger. The `does-not-support` determination is not in question at half the sample; the word "majority" is a needless credibility exposure in front of a commissioner who can count.
3. **Version 2 still carries the draft disclaimer.** `legal_disclaimer` is unchanged: *"Draft for review — not a legally binding conformance claim until reviewed and issued by RiverCity Metro Authority."* If the Authority publishes an ACR per major release, this string has to change on issue or the published document disclaims itself.

Plus the open question from section 4: whether S04 and S10 still exist as templates, and a one-line rationale in the sample record either way.

---

## 8. What this report does not say

- It is **not a conformance claim** for either cycle. The two ACRs are; this compares them.
- It says **nothing about the RideRC native app, the PDF timetables, hardware, or support documentation.** Those sit outside the web boundary in both cycles, identically, and neither document draws conclusions for them.
- It says **nothing about surfaces outside both samples** — roughly 240 of 251 URLs this cycle. Both documents are sample-scoped WCAG-EM conclusions; `supports` means no failure was observed in the sample, not that the portal conforms everywhere. This report inherits that limit exactly.
- It does **not establish that the three closed findings are fixed portal-wide** — only that they were verified absent in the current sample and in the carried-over P01 branches.
- It does **not re-check sample representativeness.** Each cycle's representativeness check is the evaluators' own; it was not re-performed here.
- It does **not evaluate Level AAA**, which is outside the engagement's target in both cycles.
- **No testing was performed for this request.** Every factual claim traces to the two delivered ACRs, the two sample records, or the delivered re-check table. Every claim that does not is marked as inference.

---

# Handoff note — engagement owner

**Re:** rcm-2026q3 → rcm-2027q1 drift report, RiverCity Metro Rider Portal
**From:** reporting desk
**Date:** 2027-02-19

The drift report above is ready. It is a document-to-document comparison only — no retesting, and the current cycle's evidence is quoted as delivered. Four things need your call before it goes to the Authority.

**Three corrections in the current ACR, all small, none affecting a determination:**

1. `evaluation_methods_used` says P01 was carried over; the engagement record says both complete processes were. I read this as the methods string being scoped to the web component (P02 is the native app), but as written the two disagree. Confirm and let me tighten the clause.
2. The re-check table calls the skip-link failure "the majority of the sample." It is 6 of 12 — exactly half. The ACR row's own phrasing, "every template now built on the legacy shell," is both accurate and more forceful. Recommend we use it in both places.
3. The legal disclaimer still reads "Draft for review" on a version-2 document. If the Authority is issuing this for the 2027.1 release, that string has to change. If it genuinely stays draft, no change — but I'd rather ask than assume.

**One open question I cannot resolve from the records:** S04 (service alerts) and S10 (accessibility policy) left the sample without a stated successor, unlike S05 → S13 and S09 → S15. Are those templates still live? If so, the drift report should say plainly that the current cycle carries no evidence for them. If they were retired from the product, the sample rationale should say that, or the Authority will read it as a coverage gap — and the accessibility policy page is a conspicuous one to have unsampled.

**How I would frame the substance if the Authority asks for the headline:**

The 2026.3 CRITICAL is closed and verified on the same surfaces that failed, which is the strongest result in the pair — a keyboard user can now buy a pass. Against that, the missing skip-link target spread from two peripheral pages to half the sample, including two templates that passed last cycle, so its promotion to MAJOR is earned on reach. Open findings dropped 7 → 5, but four of the five are repeats and three of the four current MAJORs trace to templates shipped or rebuilt between 2026-10 and 2026-12. I would resist letting "7 → 5" carry the summary.

**Two observations for the Authority's prioritisation, which is theirs and not ours to make:**

- The route-badge contrast defect (`2ab9d871`) is a single shared component, unchanged for two cycles, that has now propagated into a newly built template. It looks like the cheapest fix with the widest reach on the list, and it has had no attention while its blast radius grew.
- The autocomplete row (`44b09ce6`) improved on paper while the surface that still fails is the paratransit application form. The conformance level moved; the experience of the people most likely to need autofill did not. Worth saying out loud so the improved row is not read as the item being handled.

**One process note, offered as an observation rather than a finding:** the checkout remediation programme closed everything it targeted, and S13 — rebuilt in the same window — shipped clean, so building accessibly was clearly achievable. The defects that grew came in with template work. If the Authority wants next cycle's drift report to look different, an accessibility gate on template releases will do more than any item on the current findings list.

Ready to issue on your word once items 1–3 are settled.
